subject: English
passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• In 1955, Rosa Parks refused to give up her seat on a Montgomery city bus, sparking a bus boycott.
• The boycott aimed to protest racial segregation in public transportation.
• The boycott lasted 381 days and ended when the Supreme Court ruled bus segregation unconstitutional.
• The Montgomery boycott brought national attention to the civil rights movement.
• It established Martin Luther King Jr. as a prominent leader and inspired similar protests across the South.
prompt: The student wants to make and support a generalization about the Montgomery bus boycott. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: During the Montgomery bus boycott, Rosa Parks refused to give up her seat on a city bus, sparking a 381-day protest against racial segregation in public transportation.
choices.B: The Montgomery bus boycott had significant consequences, bringing national attention to the civil rights movement and establishing Martin Luther King Jr. as a prominent leader.
choices.C: Although the Montgomery bus boycott lasted 381 days and ended with a Supreme Court ruling, the boycott had significant consequences.
choices.D: The civil rights movement received national attention and Martin Luther King Jr. emerged as a prominent leader as a result of the Montgomery bus boycott.

explanation:
Choice B is the best answer. It makes a generalization—the boycott had significant consequences—and then supports it with evidence—the national attention and leadership emergence were results of the boycott.

Why A is incorrect:

Choice A is incorrect. This choice doesn't make a generalization about the boycott. It describes specific events from the boycott.
